title: Introduction to OSHA practice questions
description: Free Introduction to OSHA practice questions on 29 CFR 1903 and 1904. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.question: On construction work, which is a physically dispersed activity, where must the OSHA notice to employees be posted?

options.A: At the employer's corporate headquarters only
options.B: Inside each piece of heavy equipment
options.C: At the location to which employees report each day
options.D: On the employer's website

questions.explanation: For physically dispersed activities such as construction, the notice "shall be posted at the location to which employees report each day."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.2, Posting of notice; availability of the Act, regulations and applicable standards (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Where employers are engaged in activities which are physically dispersed, such as agriculture, construction, transportation, communications, and electric, gas and sanitary services, the notice or notices required by this section shall be posted at the location to which employees report each day.

questions.question: When advance notice of an inspection is allowed, how far ahead may it be given, apart from apparent imminent danger and other unusual circumstances?

options.A: Not more than 24 hours before the inspection
options.B: Not more than 7 calendar days before
options.C: Not more than 15 working days before
options.D: Not more than 30 days before

questions.explanation: Advance notice "shall not be given more than 24 hours before the inspection is scheduled to be conducted, except in apparent imminent danger situations and in other unusual circumstances."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.6, Advance notice of inspections (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Advance notice in any of the situations described in paragraph (a) of this section shall not be given more than 24 hours before the inspection is scheduled to be conducted, except in apparent imminent danger situations and in other unusual circumstances.

questions.question: Who must be given an opportunity to accompany the Compliance Safety and Health Officer during the physical inspection?

options.A: Only the employer's attorney
options.B: Only the general contractor's owner
options.C: Any member of the public who asks
options.D: A representative of the employer and a representative authorized by the employees

questions.explanation: "A representative of the employer and a representative authorized by his employees shall be given an opportunity to accompany" the officer during the physical inspection, "for the purpose of aiding such inspection."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.8, Representatives of employers and employees (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: A representative of the employer and a representative authorized by his employees shall be given an opportunity to accompany the Compliance Safety and Health Officer during the physical inspection of any workplace for the purpose of aiding such inspection.

questions.question: If an employer refuses to let the Compliance Safety and Health Officer enter, what does the officer do?

options.A: Issues an on-the-spot fine and enters anyway
options.B: Terminates the inspection or confines it to areas with no objection, and reports the refusal to the Area Director
options.C: Closes the job site until the employer agrees
options.D: Asks the local police to force entry

questions.explanation: The officer "shall terminate the inspection or confine the inspection to other areas" where no objection is raised, and "shall immediately report the refusal and the reason therefor to the Area Director."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.4, Objection to inspection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: the Safety and Health Officer shall terminate the inspection or confine the inspection to other areas, conditions, structures, machines, apparatus, devices, equipment, materials, records, or interviews concerning which no objection is raised. The Compliance Safety and Health Officer shall endeavor to ascertain the reason for such refusal, and shall immediately report the refusal and the reason therefor to the Area Director.

questions.question: An employee files a written complaint and asks that his name be kept off the copy given to the employer. What does 1903.11 say?

options.A: The complaint is rejected because it cannot be anonymous
options.B: His name and the names of employees referred to must not appear in the employer's copy
options.C: The employer may ask OSHA for the name after the inspection
options.D: His name is withheld only if a union files the complaint

questions.explanation: Upon the request of the person giving the notice, "his name and the names of individual employees referred to therein shall not appear in such copy or on any record published, released, or made available by the Department of Labor."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.11, Complaints by employees (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: except that, upon the request of the person giving such notice, his name and the names of individual employees referred to therein shall not appear in such copy or on any record published, released, or made available by the Department of Labor.

questions.question: An inspection is made because of an employee complaint. What may the inspection cover?

options.A: Only the exact hazard named in the complaint
options.B: Only the area where the complaining employee works
options.C: Only records, not physical conditions
options.D: It is not limited to matters referred to in the complaint

questions.explanation: "Inspections under this section shall not be limited to matters referred to in the complaint."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.11, Complaints by employees (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Inspections under this section shall not be limited to matters referred to in the complaint.

questions.question: How does 1903.14(f) define "imminent danger" for its employee rescue policy?

options.A: Any condition or practice that could reasonably be expected to cause death or serious physical harm before it can be abated
options.B: Any hazard that has caused an injury in the last 12 months
options.C: Any violation the employer has been cited for before
options.D: Any condition reported by two or more employees

questions.explanation: The term "imminent danger" means "the existence of any condition or practice that could reasonably be expected to cause death or serious physical harm before such condition or practice can be abated."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.14, Citations; notices of de minimis violations; policy regarding employee rescue activities (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: For purposes of this policy, the term "imminent danger" means the existence of any condition or practice that could reasonably be expected to cause death or serious physical harm before such condition or practice can be abated.

questions.question: On the basis of an inspection, a Compliance Safety and Health Officer concludes that conditions could reasonably be expected to cause death or serious physical harm immediately or before the danger can be eliminated through the Act's other enforcement procedures. Whom must the officer inform?

options.A: Only the local fire department
options.B: Only the employer's insurance carrier
options.C: The affected employees and employers, telling them a civil action to restrain the conditions is being recommended
options.D: No one until the citation is mailed

questions.explanation: The officer "shall inform the affected employees and employers of the danger and that he is recommending a civil action to restrain such conditions or practices."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.13, Imminent danger (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: he shall inform the affected employees and employers of the danger and that he is recommending a civil action to restrain such conditions or practices and for other appropriate relief in accordance with the provisions of section 13(a) of the Act.

questions.question: What is the time limit for issuing a citation under 1903.14?

options.A: 30 days after the inspection begins
options.B: 15 working days after the closing conference
options.C: 1 year after the violation is reported
options.D: 6 months following the occurrence of the alleged violation

questions.explanation: "No citation may be issued under this section after the expiration of 6 months following the occurrence of any alleged violation."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.14, Citations; notices of de minimis violations; policy regarding employee rescue activities (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: No citation may be issued under this section after the expiration of 6 months following the occurrence of any alleged violation.

questions.question: How long must a posted citation stay up?

options.A: Until the violation has been abated, or for 3 working days, whichever is later
options.B: Exactly 24 hours
options.C: Until the employer files a notice of contest
options.D: Until April 30 of the following year

questions.explanation: Each citation "shall remain posted until the violation has been abated, or for 3 working days, whichever is later." Filing a notice of contest does not affect this duty "unless and until the Review Commission issues a final order vacating the citation."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.16, Posting of citations (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Each citation, or a copy thereof, shall remain posted until the violation has been abated, or for 3 working days, whichever is later. The filing by the employer of a notice of intention to contest under § 1903.17 shall not affect his posting responsibility under this section unless and until the Review Commission issues a final order vacating the citation.

questions.question: Where must an employer post a citation it receives, where that is practicable?

options.A: In the company's annual report
options.B: In the employer's main office files only
options.C: Unedited, at or near each place an alleged violation referred to in the citation occurred
options.D: On the OSHA 300 Log

questions.explanation: The employer "shall immediately post such citation, or a copy thereof, unedited, at or near each place an alleged violation referred to in the citation occurred."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.16, Posting of citations (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Upon receipt of any citation under the Act, the employer shall immediately post such citation, or a copy thereof, unedited, at or near each place an alleged violation referred to in the citation occurred, except as provided below.

questions.question: An employer wants to contest a citation. Its written notice of intention to contest must be postmarked within what time?

options.A: 5 calendar days of the inspection
options.B: 15 working days of receiving the notice of proposed penalty
options.C: 30 calendar days of the closing conference
options.D: 6 months of the violation

questions.explanation: The notice of intention to contest "shall be postmarked within 15 working days of the receipt by the employer of the notice of proposed penalty."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.17, Employer and employee contests before the Review Commission (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Such notice of intention to contest shall be postmarked within 15 working days of the receipt by the employer of the notice of proposed penalty.

questions.question: What may an employee or employee representative contest before the Review Commission under 1903.17(b)?

options.A: That the period of time fixed in the citation for abatement is unreasonable
options.B: The amount of the proposed penalty
options.C: Whether the employer should have been cited at all
options.D: The Compliance Safety and Health Officer's choice of inspection date

questions.explanation: Employees or their representative may "file a written notice with the Area Director alleging that the period of time fixed in the citation for the abatement of the violation is unreasonable."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.17, Employer and employee contests before the Review Commission (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Any employee or representative of employees of an employer to whom a citation has been issued may, under section 10(c) of the Act, file a written notice with the Area Director alleging that the period of time fixed in the citation for the abatement of the violation is unreasonable.

questions.question: An employer requests an informal conference about a citation. What effect does this have on the 15-working-day period to file a notice of contest?

options.A: It doubles the period to 30 working days
options.B: It pauses the period until the conference ends
options.C: It cancels the citation
options.D: It does not stay the 15-working-day period

questions.explanation: "No such conference or request for such conference shall operate as a stay of any 15-working-day period for filing a notice of intention to contest."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.20, Informal conferences (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: No such conference or request for such conference shall operate as a stay of any 15-working-day period for filing a notice of intention to contest as prescribed in § 1903.17.

questions.question: When must an employer certify to OSHA that a cited violation has been abated, unless the compliance officer observed the abatement during the on-site inspection within 24 hours after the violation was identified and noted it in the citation?

options.A: Before the closing conference
options.B: Within 24 hours of receiving the citation
options.C: Within 10 calendar days after the abatement date
options.D: At the end of the calendar year

questions.explanation: "Within 10 calendar days after the abatement date, the employer must certify to OSHA (the Agency) that each cited violation has been abated," except as provided in paragraph (c)(2).

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.19, Abatement verification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Within 10 calendar days after the abatement date, the employer must certify to OSHA (the Agency) that each cited violation has been abated, except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) of this section. (2) The employer is not required to certify abatement if the OSHA Compliance Officer, during the on-site portion of the inspection: (i) Observes, within 24 hours after a violation is identified, that abatement has occurred; and (ii) Notes in the citation that abatement has occurred.

questions.question: A company had 10 or fewer employees at all times during the last calendar year, and neither OSHA nor the Bureau of Labor Statistics has informed it in writing that it must keep records. What does Part 1904 require?

options.A: It must keep full OSHA 300, 300-A and 301 records
options.B: It need not keep OSHA injury and illness records, but must still report fatalities, in-patient hospitalizations, amputations and eye losses
options.C: It is exempt from all of Part 1904, including reporting
options.D: It must keep records only for supervisors

questions.explanation: Such a company does "not need to keep OSHA injury and illness records unless OSHA or the Bureau of Labor Statistics informs you in writing," but all covered employers "must report to OSHA any work-related incident that results in a fatality, the in-patient hospitalization of one or more employees, an employee amputation, or an employee loss of an eye."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.1, Partial exemption for employers with 10 or fewer employees (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: If your company had 10 or fewer employees at all times during the last calendar year, you do not need to keep OSHA injury and illness records unless OSHA or the Bureau of Labor Statistics informs you in writing that you must keep records under § 1904.41 or § 1904.42. However, as required by § 1904.39, all employers covered by the OSH Act must report to OSHA any work-related incident that results in a fatality, the in-patient hospitalization of one or more employees, an employee amputation, or an employee loss of an eye.

questions.question: How soon must a recordable injury or illness be entered on the OSHA 300 Log and 301 Incident Report?

options.A: Within seven (7) calendar days of receiving information that it occurred
options.B: Within 8 hours
options.C: By February 1 of the next year
options.D: Within 30 days of the employee returning to work

questions.explanation: "You must enter each recordable injury or illness on the OSHA 300 Log and 301 Incident Report within seven (7) calendar days of receiving information that a recordable injury or illness has occurred."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.29, Forms (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: You must enter each recordable injury or illness on the OSHA 300 Log and 301 Incident Report within seven (7) calendar days of receiving information that a recordable injury or illness has occurred.

questions.question: When must the annual summary of injuries and illnesses be posted, and until when?

options.A: By January 1, until March 31
options.B: By March 1, until June 30
options.C: Within 7 days of year end, until December 31
options.D: No later than February 1 of the following year, until April 30

questions.explanation: "You must post the summary no later than February 1 of the year following the year covered by the records and keep the posting in place until April 30."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.32, Annual summary (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: You must post the summary no later than February 1 of the year following the year covered by the records and keep the posting in place until April 30.

questions.question: How long must the OSHA 300 Log, the privacy case list, the annual summary and the 301 forms be saved?

options.A: One year after the case closes
options.B: Five (5) years following the end of the calendar year the records cover
options.C: Ten years after the employee leaves
options.D: Until the next OSHA inspection

questions.explanation: These records must be saved "for five (5) years following the end of the calendar year that these records cover."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.33, Retention and updating (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: You must save the OSHA 300 Log, the privacy case list (if one exists), the annual summary, and the OSHA 301 Incident Report forms for five (5) years following the end of the calendar year that these records cover.

questions.question: A work-related incident results in an employee's in-patient hospitalization (a formal admission for care or treatment) on the same day as the incident. Within what time after the hospitalization must the employer report it to OSHA?

options.A: Within eight (8) hours
options.B: Within seven (7) calendar days
options.C: Within twenty-four (24) hours
options.D: Within thirty (30) days

questions.explanation: "Within twenty-four (24) hours after the in-patient hospitalization of one or more employees or an employee's amputation or an employee's loss of an eye," the employer must report it to OSHA. A fatality must be reported within eight (8) hours.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.39, Reporting fatalities, hospitalizations, amputations, and losses of an eye as a result of work-related incidents to OSHA (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Within eight (8) hours after the death of any employee as a result of a work-related incident, you must report the fatality to the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), U.S. Department of Labor. (2) Within twenty-four (24) hours after the in-patient hospitalization of one or more employees or an employee's amputation or an employee's loss of an eye, as a result of a work-related incident, you must report the in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or loss of an eye to OSHA.
